title: age-based-deadline-batcher: add aging tokens and soft-preemption to prevent starvation
author: Diego Alvarez
description: Motivation: Continuous batching currently favors short, high-throughput queries and can starve long-running or low-frequency request classes under skewed workloads. This PR introduces an age-based deadline bucket and a soft-preemption policy that raises effective priority for long-waiting batches and uses lightweight preemption signals to reduce starvation while preserving batching efficiency. Summary of changes: 1) deadline_scheduler: add per-request "age_token" tracking and an adaptive deadline bucket hierarchy. Requests accumulate age_tokens as they wait; tokens are decayed on successful batching. The scheduler now computes an effective_deadline = base_deadline - f(age_tokens) where f scales with recent per-queue latency history. 2) soft_preempt: implement cooperative preemption: when a high-age bucket exceeds a configurable threshold the scheduler inserts a soft_preempt marker at the head of the next schedule window; workers check for the marker and will allow priority windows to pass instead of blocking long-running low-priority batches. This avoids hard kill/requeue cycles. 3) kv_cache: introduce affinity hints for cached KV slices to improve cache hits for large-context requests that used to be repeatedly reloaded, reducing tail latency for aged requests. 4) telemetry and knobs: add metrics for aged_waits, preempt_signals_sent, and preempt_cooperative_successes; expose runtime flags: redwood.batcher.age_threshold_ms, redwood.batcher.soft_preempt_fraction, redwood.batcher.age_decay_half_life_ms. 5) tests and benchmarks: add integration test to validate no starvation under a synthetic skewed mix and end-to-end perf bench showing P99 client latency improvement under skew. Design notes and rationale: - We prefer soft cooperative preemption to avoid expensive requeue/restart semantics that blow away KV caches and waste GPU compute. - Age tokens are lightweight integer counters accumulated per-request; they avoid timer-based complexity while still capturing relative wait time. - The effective_deadline adjustment uses an exponential scaling function tuned to target P99 SLOs per workload class. Example pseudo-snippet (from scheduler): if (age_tokens > SOFT_PREEMPT_TOKENS) { effective_priority += age_tokens / SOFT_PREEMPT_SCALE; } Worker participation example (pseudocode): "if (schedule_window.has_soft_preempt_marker && current_batch_can_yield) { yield_to_preempt_window(); }" Backwards compatibility and rollout: - Feature is behind a runtime flag (default off for existing clusters). - A staged rollout is recommended: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with metrics checks on p50/p95/p99 and batch efficiency. - Added an automatic rollback guard: if global batch efficiency drops >8% for 5m while p99 improves <2%, the gate disables soft_preempt automatically. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for age token accounting and decay rules. - Integration test: skewed-ttl-benchmark reproducer (10k qps, 90% tiny, 10% large) asserts no queue for large requests exceeds 250ms extra wait at P99 after warmup. - Microbench: under synthetic skew we measure: baseline P99 = 980ms, PR P99 = 320ms, avg token increase of 2.5 for aged requests, batch utilization delta: -3.6% at most during transient. Files changed (high level): - redwood/runtime/batching/deadline_scheduler.rs: new age token logic, deadline buckets, scheduler config parsing. - redwood/runtime/batching/soft_preempt.rs: cooperative preemption marker management and worker-side yield helpers. - redwood/runtime/caching/kv_affinity.rs: KV slice affinity hints and tracing. - redwood/runtime/tests/batcher_integration_test.rs: synthetic skew test and metrics assertions. - redwood/docs/ops/batcher_tuning.md: documentation for knobs and rollout steps. - redwood/benchmarks/bench_batcher_aging.yaml: bench harness config. Review thread (high level): - Maya Chen (reviewer): "Great direction; can we ensure the age token increment path is non-blocking and cheap?" — Diego: "Age tokens are incremented in the scheduler enqueue path using an atomic fetch_add; moved heavy math to scheduler tick so enqueue stays fast." - Rina Okafor: "Concern about KV affinity causing imbalanced placement on NUMA nodes." — Diego: "Added a fallback heuristic: affinity hints are advisory; the placement respects current gpu/memory load and falls back to round-robin when imbalance detected." - Liam O'Neill: "Bench numbers look optimistic; request end-to-end traces?" — Diego: "Attached representative traces to the CI artifact and added a reproducible harness config to benchmarks dir." CI and stability: - Initial CI run failed two flakey tests in runtime caching; fixed race in kv_affinity initialization and re-ran. Current CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, benchmark-smoke) and E2E bench artifacts uploaded. Merge/Changelog: - Merge method: squash/merge. - Changelog entry added under Unreleased: "batcher: add age-based deadlines and cooperative preemption to reduce starvation under skewed workloads (opt-in via runtime flag)." Rollout recommendations and monitoring: - Watch metrics: redwood.batcher.aged_waits.P99, redwood.batcher.preempt_signals_sent.rate, infra.batch_efficiency. - Recommended alert: if preempt_signals_sent rate exceeds 25% sustained and batch_efficiency < 60% for 10m, investigate. Risk and mitigation: - Risk: mis-tuned thresholds may reduce throughput. Mitigation: default off, staged rollout, auto-rollback guard. - Risk: interaction with Dedicated autoscaler; mitigation: added integration test in canary with autoscaler enabled. Additional notes: - This PR intentionally avoids hard requeue or forced task abortion semantics to preserve KV cache benefits for large-context generations. - Future work: per-customer adaptive thresholds and ML-driven tuning based on workload fingerprinting.
